not_rules.quote:
Use them to:
[9efd9789d074] LI  show direct speech and the quoted work of other writers

not_rules.note: Permission to use quotation marks instead of italics (G-3).
not_rules.quote:
You can use quotation marks instead of italics to make words stand out from your sentence. Examples include:
[d6089f7a8cbb] LI  a technical term on its first mention in a non-technical document
[d6aeef38234f] LI  a word or phrase that has been coined or that you’re using in a specific sense
[3a6f9b855019] LI  colloquial words, nicknames, slang, or ironic or humorous words and phrases, in formal writing.
You don’t usually need to repeat the quotation marks the next time you use the word. They might be useful if the next mention is a long way from the first.

covers.quote: Quote direct speech in single quote marks
Short quotations of direct speech are enclosed in single quotation marks.
For quotations within quotations, use double quotation marks inside single ones.

examples.note: Direct speech enclosed in single quote marks.

parts.quote: ‘Yes, that’s all that happened,’ she replied.

examples.note: Direct speech enclosed in single quote marks.

parts.quote: The opposition leader asked, ‘But where’s the money going to come from?’

examples.note: Double quotation marks used inside single quotation marks for a quote within a quote.

parts.quote: He also wrote, ‘The decisions of the department for “major procurement” were always political choices.’

rules.quote: Double quotation marks aren’t Australian Government style. Use them only for quotations within quotations.
rules.violation_condition: double quotation marks used for direct speech or titles, rather than single quotation marks, outside of quotations within quotations
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: Consolidated general rule on single quote marks for quotes and double quotes only for quotes within quotes.

examples.note: Ellipsis retains original meaning.

parts.quote: He said, ‘I don’t agree with the proposal …’

examples.note: Ellipsis distorts original meaning from negative to positive.

parts.quote: He said, ‘I … agree with the proposal.’

rules.quote: If you use ellipses for omitted words, ensure that the omission won’t mislead readers about the content or tone of the source you’re quoting.
rules.violation_condition: an omission indicated by an ellipsis that distorts or misleads about the original meaning, content, or tone
rules.why: Specific rule on not misleading readers when using ellipses in direct quotations.

covers.quote: If you paraphrase omitted material, place the paraphrasing in square brackets.

examples.note: Added specific detail in square brackets.

parts.quote: ‘The [Queensland] government agrees.’

examples.note: Paraphrased text placed in square brackets.

parts.quote: ‘They all listened to [the new manager’s] speech.’

rules.quote: If the quotation needs the information for context, add specific detail in square brackets.
rules.violation_condition: editorial context added to a quotation without enclosing it in square brackets
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Rule requiring editorial insertions and paraphrases in quotes to be bracketed.

examples.note: Italicised 'sic' in non-italicised brackets following the error.

parts.quote: The email read, ‘At the time, the population of Sydney was much higher than Melberne [sic].’

rules.quote: To show the error is in the original, insert an italicised ‘sic’ in non-italicised square brackets after the error.
rules.violation_condition: sic inserted to indicate an original error without italicising 'sic' or without enclosing it in non-italicised square brackets directly after the error
rules.why: Formatting specification for indicating errors in original quotes.

covers.quote: If the US material uses the US conventions for quotation marks, you can update them to the Australian convention.

examples.note: Australian style with single outer quotes and retained original capitalisation.

parts.quote: The President said, ‘The Prime Minister told me “No”, so I’m working on an updated plan.’

rules.quote: In quoted material use the original spelling of the quoted material, even if it uses US spellings such as ‘color’. The capitalisation of words must also be the same as in the original.
rules.violation_condition: spelling or capitalisation in quoted material altered from the original source
when: You can update quotation marks in US material to the Australian convention (single quotation marks).
rules.why: G-2, G-3: Rule requiring retention of original spelling and capitalisation in quotes, with quotation mark convention update recorded under when.

covers.quote: Format long quotes as block quotations with no quotation marks
Don’t use quotation marks for long quotations. Instead, use block quotations.

examples.note: Block quotation without quotation marks.

parts.quote: As Templeton (2019) writes:

According to the ACT Auditor-General, the transport benefits from the project are projected to be lower than the costs. She noted other benefits that had been included by the ACT Government to justify the project.

rules.quote: Don’t use quotation marks to identify the quoted material – the formatting does that instead. Block quotations should also be coded with the HTML <blockquote> element.
rules.specification: Applies to quotations that are longer than about 30 words.
rules.violation_condition: a block quotation enclosed in quotation marks, or formatted without <blockquote> HTML coding in web content
when: Applies to long quotations (longer than about 30 words).
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Prohibits quotation marks on block quotes and prescribes HTML blockquote element.

examples.note: Opening quote at the start of each paragraph, closing quote only at the end of the last paragraph.

parts.quote: Dr Nicoll said, ‘My experience as a public servant helped me learn how to run workshops.
‘My experience also helps me make my workshops practical.’

rules.quote:
To include several paragraphs of quoted speech without the attribution tag, such as in a media release, use a quotation mark:
[a4615372a8db] LI  at the beginning of each paragraph
[108b35dd751c] LI  at the end of the last paragraph only.
rules.violation_condition: a multi-paragraph direct quote formatted with a closing quotation mark at the end of paragraphs other than the final one, or missing an opening quotation mark at the start of each paragraph
when: When including several paragraphs of quoted speech without an attribution tag (such as in media releases).
rules.why: Special convention for multi-paragraph quotations in runs of text.

covers.quote: Write speech in transcripts and plays with no quotation marks
The same applies for questions and answers (Q&As).

examples.note: Direct speech in transcripts without quotation marks.

parts.quote: Senator MARCELLUS: Look at the latest report. These results aren’t great.
Dr BERNARDO: I’ve seen this happen before. It looks like we might be over budget.

examples.note: Q&A format without quotation marks.

parts.quote: Q. Have you ever been convicted of an offence, other than a parking or speeding offence?
A. No.

rules.quote: Quotation marks are unnecessary in transcripts and plays if the name of the speaker comes before the direct speech.
rules.violation_condition: quotation marks used around dialogue in transcripts, plays, or Q&A where the speaker's name or label precedes the speech
when: When the name of the speaker (or Q/A label) precedes the direct speech.
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Rule eliminating quotation marks when speaker tags/labels precede the text.

covers.quote: Refer to certain kinds of titles using quotation marks

examples.note: Chapter title enclosed in single quotation marks.

parts.quote: Read the chapter titled ‘Number and natural language’ in The innate mind: structure and contents. It describes how people learn to recognise numbers.

rules.quote:
When referring to these titles, use quotation marks in references and citations:
[bddbf992ead0] LI  a chapter in a book or report
[2c54a09a97c2] LI  an article in a periodical
[af50f2697aac] LI  an essay
[8dcf15b4d4e4] LI  a lecture
[b48bebc4be2a] LI  a poem
[edb78910c695] LI  a song.
rules.violation_condition: titles of chapters, periodical articles, essays, lectures, poems, or songs written without single quotation marks in references and citations
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Rule specifying which work titles take quotation marks.

covers.quote: Keep quoted punctuation marks in the quote
The same rule applies for directly quoted speech followed by the attribution.

examples.note: Question mark is part of the quoted question and sits inside quote marks.

parts.quote: ‘Is it okay to ask a colleague out for a coffee?’ I asked the HR section.

examples.note: Question mark inside quote marks.

parts.quote: He asked, ‘Has it arrived?’

examples.note: Comma inside quote marks when followed by attribution.

parts.quote: ‘It has arrived,’ said the manager.

rules.quote: If the punctuation mark is part of the quoted text, place the punctuation mark before the closing quotation mark.
rules.violation_condition: punctuation that belongs to the quoted text placed outside the closing quotation mark
when: When the punctuation mark is part of the quoted text or directly quoted speech followed by attribution.
rules.why: G-1, G-2: Rule governing punctuation that belongs to quoted text.

examples.note: Full stop follows closing quotation mark.

parts.quote: She said that it was ‘time to start work’.

examples.note: Comma follows closing quotation mark.

parts.quote: Many things have been called ‘the new black’, but they usually fade to grey.

examples.note: Question mark follows closing quotation mark.

parts.quote: Did the complainant at any time ask you to ‘Please turn down the noise’?

rules.quote: If the punctuation mark is part of the sentence outside the quoted text, it follows the closing quotation mark.
rules.violation_condition: punctuation belonging to the surrounding sentence placed inside closing quotation marks
rules.why: Punctuation rule for sentence-level punctuation outside quoted fragments.

examples.note: Quote marks inside parentheses.

parts.quote: His stirring speech (‘We shall never surrender’) galvanised the UK and its allies.

examples.note: Quote marks inside dashes.

parts.quote: His stirring speech – ‘We shall never surrender’ – galvanised the UK and its allies.

examples.note: Quote marks inside commas.

parts.quote: His stirring speech, ‘We shall never surrender’, galvanised the UK and its allies.

rules.quote: Quoted material can appear as parenthetical information, enclosed in parentheses, dashes or commas. In these cases, place the quotation marks inside the sentence punctuation.
rules.violation_condition: parentheses, dashes, or commas placed inside quotation marks when the quote itself is parenthetical information
when: When quoted material appears as parenthetical information.
rules.why: Specific rule positioning quotation marks inside parenthetical punctuation.

examples.note: Full stop inside quotation mark.

parts.quote: She said, ‘It’s time to start work.’

examples.note: Full stop inside final quotation mark.

parts.quote: ‘I have the final figures,’ the manager said. ‘This will ruin our bottom line.’

rules.quote: If the quotation ends a sentence or is a sentence in its own right, place the final full stop before the final quotation mark.
rules.violation_condition: a full stop placed after the closing quotation mark when the quotation is a complete sentence or ends the sentence
when: When the quotation is a sentence in its own right or ends the sentence.
rules.why: Placement rule for full stops terminating quoted complete sentences.

examples.note: Only exclamation mark used.

parts.quote: The Speaker called ‘Order!’

examples.note: Only question mark used.

parts.quote: Did you hear him say, ‘That’s unlikely’?

examples.note: Both exclamation mark and full stop used.

parts.quote: The Speaker called ‘Order!’.

examples.note: Both full stop and question mark used.

parts.quote: Did you hear him say, ‘That’s unlikely.’?

rules.quote: Sometimes, there are 2 punctuation marks – one for the quotation and one for the sentence. Decide which is stronger and use it. Don’t use both punctuation marks.
rules.violation_condition: two conflicting terminal punctuation marks used together at a closing quotation mark (e.g. '.?' or '!.')
rules.why: Explicit prohibition against doubling punctuation marks at a quotation boundary.

examples.note: Quotation marks in roman font around italic text.

parts.quote: She described it as ‘weird’.

rules.quote: The surrounding text determines the font (roman, italic, or bold) of the quotation marks. If the content inside the quotation marks is in italics, but the sentence is in roman, use roman for the quotation marks.
rules.violation_condition: quotation marks styled in italic or bold when the surrounding sentence text is in roman font
rules.why: Font styling rule for quotation mark glyphs.
